correctness.rationale: Put m=n−1 and label a word supported on i<j by (a,b)=(i,j−1). Its weight-one descendants have labels a,b, coinciding only for a loop. With t loops and e other words, disjointness gives t+2e≤m. Consecutive loops collide in the adjacent weight-two output, so t≤ceil(m/2), giving the upper bound including n=2. The odd loops and even pairs (4k+2,4k+4) attain it: their weight-one labels are disjoint; weight-two loop outputs have gap 1, while selected nonloops have gaps 2 or 3 and disjoint first-coordinate sets for different k. The code with n=2 is {11}. An independent finite check enumerated all weight-two words, deleted each of the n positions and deduplicated the results, then exactly maximized a clique in the graph with adjacency defined by disjoint deletion sets. The maxima for n=2 through 10 were 1,1,2,3,4,4,5,6,7. This is corroboration; the packing and construction prove the unbounded claim. The supplied script was inspected as text, not run.
